🇲🇽💰 <u>MEXICO'S 2027 BUDGET TEST: CUT THE DEFICIT WITHOUT CUTTING THE FUTURE</u>

El Financiero reports: the 2027 Economic Package will test the government's ability to reduce the deficit without sacrificing investment. BNP Paribas chief economist for Mexico Pamela Díaz Loubet: the risk is "that fiscal consolidation comes at the cost of investment, because that ends up affecting potential growth."

BNP projects public-sector financing needs at 4.3% of GDP in 2027, above Hacienda's 3.5% target; Mifel sees 4.5% for 2026 and 4.2% for 2027. Rating agencies will be watching the debt trajectory and Pemex support.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>SEP OPENS CALL FOR YOUNG PROFESSIONALS TO JOIN MEXICO'S NEW NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL SYSTEM</u>

El Soberano reports: Mexico's SEP opened recruitment for Guides and Promoters at the new Bachillerato Nacional Margarita Maza — university graduates aged 22 to 29 who will provide pedagogical, psychoemotional, cultural and sports accompaniment to students.

SEP chief Mario Delgado announced the registry as part of building equitable, inclusive, violence-free schools — another brick in the 4T's reconstruction of public upper-secondary education.

🇲🇽🏅 <u>SHEINBAUM RAISES ATHLETE SCHOLARSHIPS AND REWARDS ALL 407 CENTRAL AMERICAN GAMES MEDALS</u>

Contralínea reports: starting January 2027, Mexico's athletes get increased scholarships, and every one of the 407 medals won at the Santo Domingo 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games — 167 gold, 125 silver, 115 bronze — will be rewarded, President Sheinbaum announced.

"They delivered a great result and they deserve it, simple as that," she said. Conade chief Rommel Pacheco credited the High Performance Plan: 1 billion pesos for preparation, 50+ federations backed, 300+ coaches professionalized, 60 million pesos to the Olympic Committee.

Three-time Central American champions.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO SETS SECOND NATIONAL EARTHQUAKE DRILL FOR SEPTEMBER 19 — FIRST TIME ON A SATURDAY</u>

Contralínea reports: Mexico's second Simulacro Nacional of 2026 will take place September 19 at noon — for the first time on a Saturday, so families can participate from home and build household emergency plans.

The date marks the anniversaries of the 1985 and 2017 earthquakes. The drill will incorporate 58 new seismic monitoring stations, announced UNAM Geophysics Institute director José Luis Macías alongside federal authorities.

A country that lives with earthquakes prepares as one.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE US DRONES AND ANTI-DRONE SYSTEMS AGAINST CARTELS</u>

La Jornada reports: Mexico's Sedena will be able to acquire drones and counter-drone technology under a Declaration of Intent signed with the US on August 11, during the visit of US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll. Ambassador Ronald Johnson highlighted the agreement alongside Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch: "Our defense cooperation continues to strengthen."

As cartels escalate their use of drones, Mexico is building its own counter-capability — through its armed forces, under Mexican command.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO CITY TOLL HIGHWAYS TRIPLED THEIR PROFITS IN SIX YEARS — CITY HALL GOT 1%</u>

La Jornada reports: the three private concessionaires running Mexico City's urban toll highways saw gross revenue jump from 1,266 million pesos in 2019 to 3,898 million in 2024 — 15,888 million pesos collected over six years. The city government's share over that entire period: 158.9 million pesos. One percent.

The Supervía Poniente alone raised its take 164.9%.

The neoliberal concession model in a single number: the public provides the demand, the operator keeps 99 centavos of every peso.
